PullRequest.Title: accounts: read the default account as a GitHub account through one accessor
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

## What this changes

Adds `asGitHubAccount(account)` in `src/vs/base/common/defaultAccount.ts` and moves the code that uses the default account to make GitHub requests onto it.

**There is no behavior change.** Every default account is a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise account, so the accessor returns the account it is given. Each call site reads the account through `asGitHubAccount`.

## Why

Many places treat "the default account" and "a GitHub account" as the same thing: they take the account's authentication provider and session to get a GitHub token, use its name as a GitHub login, or read its enterprise flag. That is correct while every default account is a GitHub account. This change gives those readers one place to ask the question, so that a default account that is not a GitHub account can be introduced later without each of them sending the wrong session to GitHub.

This pull request does not introduce such an account. It does not change `IDefaultAccount`, the entitlement state, the policy services or `DefaultAccountProvider`. On its own it is an accessor with one branch; it is meant to be read together with the change that gives it a second one.

## What moved, and the rule

The rule: a reader moves if it uses the account's authentication provider, session, name or enterprise flag to make a GitHub request, or to decide something about GitHub.

| Reader | What it uses the account for |
|---|---|
| `WorkbenchGitHubService` | Session for the default GitHub client |
| `CopilotConnectorsService`, `CustomizationMarketplaceWorkbenchService` | Session and account identity for connector and marketplace requests |
| `getGitHubEnvironmentSessions`, `MissionControlSharingService` | Session for environment sharing |
| `WelcomeName` | Session for the GitHub profile name |
| `CloudAutomationStore`, `GitHubCloudAutomationStore` | Account name as a GitHub login; enterprise flag |
| `ChatEntitlementRequests.getSessions` | Session used to sign up for Copilot Free |
| `GitHubGalleryAccountProvider.checkAccess` | Enterprise flag |

Left alone on purpose:

- Code that forwards the sign-in to the Agent Host (`agentHostAuth.ts` and the files around it). It sends whatever the user signed in with. `agentHostAutoTierScope.ts` is in this group although it finds a session by id the same way a moved reader does: it decides what the Agent Host is told about the signed-in account.
- Surfaces that show who is signed in (title bar, account menus, setup). `agentFeedbackEditorWidget.ts` is in this group: it shows the account name as `@name` for the comment author. That formatting assumes a GitHub login and is a judgment call.
- The policy services and experiment assignment.
- `DefaultAccountProvider`, which builds the account.

## How the list of readers was checked

As a local experiment that is not part of this change, I renamed the four sign-in fields of `IDefaultAccount` (`authenticationProvider`, `accountName`, `sessionId`, `enterprise`), ran the type check, and classified every error in production code.

| | Files | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| Before this change | 25 | 117 |
| After this change | 15 | 48 |

The 48 that remain are the account's writer (8), surfaces that show the signed-in identity (12), Agent Host sign-in forwarding (19), the policy services (4) and experiment assignment (5). None is a reader that makes GitHub requests. The type is a subset of `IDefaultAccount` and does not stop new code from reading the fields directly; the experiment is how to find such code.

## A note for a later change

`asGitHubAccount` returns `undefined` both when there is no default account and, in the future, when the account is not a GitHub account. Three readers fall back to any GitHub session when there is no default account: `getGitHubEnvironmentSessions`, `MissionControlSharingService._withdraw` and `ChatEntitlementRequests.getSessions`. In the first two the accessor is applied inside the existing "there is a default account" branch, so they would report the wrong kind of account instead of falling back. The third is unchanged and would fall back. Whoever introduces a default account that is not a GitHub account needs to test each reader for that case.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the 11 changed files: passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`, then `scripts\test.bat --run <file>` for 23 test files covering each touched module plus the default account and account policy suites: 1218 passing, 0 failing. No existing test was edited.
- The accessor has no test of its own, because it returns its argument. The evidence that nothing changed is the existing suites passing unedited and the experiment above.

Live check, on a local build of the first commit of this branch in the Agents window, with a new empty profile and default settings, signing in with a GitHub.com account:

- Before sign-in the window showed the signed-out banner and the Agent Host's model listing failed as not authenticated.
- After sign-in the Agent Host log showed the authentication calls for the GitHub API and a successful model listing; the banner went away and the title bar showed the account.
- The welcome greeting showed the GitHub profile name, which goes through `WelcomeName` and the default client of `WorkbenchGitHubService`, two of the readers this change moves.
- One chat message completed.

The second commit renames the accessor and tidies the moved call sites; it was not checked live again. Also not checked live: a GitHub Enterprise account, the editor window, and the other moved readers (connectors, marketplace, environment sharing, cloud automations, Copilot Free sign-up, the extension gallery check). Those are covered by the unit tests above only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve the default GitHub API client and respond to account/session changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Client acquisition waits for account initialization when necessary, provider sessions, and credential resolution before API consumers proceed. The new accessor returns the existing account reference synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve authentication sessions from the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session retrieval per options resolution absent concurrent session-version changes; existing credential checks may retrieve sessions again when requests are sent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls, arguments, session filtering, and version retry loop; account fields were read directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session retrieval precedes successful client acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Determined by existing API consumers; eligible identical GETs share in-flight requests. The accessor adds no API calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same transport, request keys, coalescing, rate limits, and shared queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: API consumers await their requested data; acquiring an account reference does not itself fetch resource collections.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Client acquisitions and authentication events; session selection scans the provider's sessions, not repositories or result rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing GitHub runtime queue bounds active requests to 12 globally, 10 per account, and 8 per caller by default. No scheduling or admission changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: DefaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount waits on a shared initialization barrier and returns stored state. Existing client references, authorization keys, and invalidation predicates remain equivalent. The credential provider records grants but still retrieves sessions on each getSessions invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the accessor is only account ?? undefined, with no runtime imports, allocation, or I/O; all changed client keys and predicates preserve their values.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider activation and API latency vary; no measurements were taken.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: request frequency, authorization identity, invalidation, and concurrency are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse, authorize, connect, and disconnect Copilot connectors.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Catalog refresh awaits authentication and a catalog request. Connecting additionally waits for authorization, a mutation, and serial polling; live Agent Host refresh may be awaited after connected membership changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Get/create authentication sessions and refresh live Agent Host connector sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getSessions per getAuthentication call, optional createSession when required permissions are missing, and existing Agent Host refreshes on authorization/membership changes or explicit actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same calls under the same conditions; accessor wrapping leaves identity comparison results unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication gates connector requests; some action completion paths await the Agent Host refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the whole connector catalog and mutate a selected connector connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalog request per refresh, one connection mutation when needed, and one catalog request per sequential polling iteration until completion or the existing deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical collection request, polling, timeout, retry/reset bounds, and transport settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog visibility and action completion await the corresponding responses.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User operations, catalog polling iterations, affected authentication sessions, and catalog size. Catalog retrieval is one collection request, not one request per connector.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authorization remains single-flight. Poll iterations are awaited sequentially. Concurrent operations retain existing runtime queue limits; no added fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing account-identity JSON is unchanged. Authorization promises coalesce; API clients are reused for matching authorization. Catalog reset and cancellation triggers remain equivalent. Catalog GET uses ETags but explicitly disables transport coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every changed identity helper receives the same object and serializes the same four fields; no cache invalidation or cancellation condition changes for current account types.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size, user consent time, and number of polls vary; none of those inputs are increased by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression or concrete performance fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh customization marketplace sources and curated browse sections after authentication changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed event filter can invalidate browse caches and cancel active browse work. Browse sections deliver incremental cached/progress results and await provider feeds for completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three provider feed calls per eligible browse-sections invocation, including warm-cache revalidation; each result defaults to a 30-item page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same three calls and cache invalidations. Direct account access and accessor-wrapped access produce the same event-filter result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cached/progress sections may appear earlier; final completion waits for the feeds or their existing timeout behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authentication events and three fixed editorial feed slots, rather than one call per displayed marketplace item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three feed requests run via existing Promise.all, each with existing timeout/cancellation handling. No concurrency changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same provider/session-match predicate clears the same caches. Cached sections can be shown immediately, but the existing implementation still refreshes all three feeds on warm as well as cold calls; the PR does not introduce that behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only runtime change here wraps an existing account read in the identity accessor, leaving event cardinality and cache lifecycle unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend feed latency and runtime-internal network work are provider-dependent; the unchanged IPC invocation count and scheduling are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; existing warm-cache refresh behavior is outside the diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable, reconfigure, or withdraw GitHub environment sharing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enabling awaits account/session lookup, filesystem validation, and Agent Host configuration. Withdrawal may retrieve the existing environment ID and owner sessions before issuing its configuration call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read authentication sessions and optionally create a scoped session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: With a selected matching default account, two getSessions calls for configuration; without one, one scoped call. At most one optional createSession per helper call. Withdrawal fallback performs one session retrieval when owner recovery is needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same branches, call counts, account filtering, and fallback rules for all currently representable accounts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Owner and permission resolution precede configuration or withdrawal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate local drive roots and project directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Windows checks up to 26 roots with stat and conditional realpath; project validation performs one stat per local project. Non-Windows root enumeration needs no drive scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical checks on the identical configuration path; account change comparisons schedule the same updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Filesystem checks must finish before the configuration payload is sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure or withdraw Mission Control through the Agent Host management channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration call per successful attempt; withdrawal issues one call when an owner is known and may first query the environment ID when it is not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same management calls and payload construction; no extra process start, configuration attempt, or remote registration is caused by the accessor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sharing enablement or withdrawal waits for management completion, which delegates to the existing Mission Control environment service.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected account; its sessions; local project folders; at most 26 candidate Windows drive roots per configuration attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces updates and Throttler serializes configuration work. Drive checks and project checks use existing Promise.all; interactive transient failures retain the existing maximum of two retries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account/session ownership, stored sharing enablement, generation guards, and known account ID are unchanged. A known owner avoids withdrawal's fallback lookup. Missing permission sessions may trigger the existing interactive sign-in path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: comparisons still inspect identical provider/name/session values and preserve the original stored default account.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and remote-registration latency vary by platform and projects; those costs are pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: neither filesystem fan-out nor IPC frequency is introduced or amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve the visible welcome greeting from the GitHub profile.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Profile resolution occurs asynchronously only while the surface is enabled and no configured name overrides it. The greeting's profile value waits for authentication and the profile request; rendering is not synchronously blocked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read authentication sessions and resolve credentials for an account API client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One explicit session lookup per uncached profile fetch, plus existing credential-resolution lookups; zero profile-fetch lookups for a cached key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cache keys and cache misses caused identical session/client operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes profile lookup, off the synchronous rendering path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical profile read per uncached provider/session key, retried only after the existing failed-fetch eviction behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same visibility guards, shared promise, request, priority, and disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the asynchronous profile-derived name awaits the response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct provider/session keys and visible welcome-name consumers; concurrent consumers of the same key share one promise.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single shared profile promise per account key; requests for different keys may overlap under the existing GitHub queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The module-level provider/session promise cache is unchanged. Successful and empty results remain cached; rejected fetches remove the key for retry. Hidden or explicitly named surfaces still skip fetching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the accessor preserves account identity and cache-key fields exactly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network duration and number of session identities vary, but neither is changed here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; existing caching and lazy visibility gating are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize, refresh, render, and manage cloud automations and run history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enabled GitHub.com accounts create the existing store and start asynchronous refresh. Refresh awaits repository discovery, configuration, definition reads, then applicable history work. Rendering descriptors only transforms already loaded entries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve local recent workspaces using .git metadata and config reads, without spawning git.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution per local recent workspace during discovery; each resolution searches at most 50 ancestors and conditionally reads worktree/config metadata. Remote GitHub workspace URIs bypass this resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same recent-workspace iteration and filesystem resolver; no increased discovery attempts or store reconstruction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repository discovery finishes before the corresponding catalogue requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire an authenticated GitHub account client through existing session/credential retrieval.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One memoized client acquisition per store lifetime, with existing retry after rejection and invalidation/reset behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same memoization, cancellation, invalidation, and account eligibility.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/githubCloudAutomationStore.ts:refreshRepositories, listDefinitions, refreshHistory, create, update, delete, run
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read repository capabilities, automation definitions, runs and task details, and perform requested mutations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration read per deduplicated repository; eligible repositories have paginated lists capped at 10 pages of 100 and one detail read per summary. History reads once per included automation plus details for active tasks. Mutations retain their existing preflight and write calls. Transport caching/coalescing may reduce actual eligible read traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical repository grouping, pagination, batching, history filtering, mutations, and request queue. The changed history ownership comparison only runs on the existing 404 path and yields the same result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalogue/history availability or individual mutation completion awaits these operations; initial refresh is asynchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplicated repository keys from remembered/target/recent repositories; automation summaries per repository; included history entries and active tasks; recent local workspace paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Store operations remain sequenced. Repository discovery and configuration loops are serial; definition detail reads run in batches of five; history entries use Limiter(4), with active-task details awaited inside each entry. Repository-picker capability checks retain batches of five.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account-scoped storage keys and descriptor IDs are unchanged. Client acquisition and definition refresh remain single-flight. Repository capability successes and retry-delayed failures remain cached. Explicit catalogue refresh still rechecks repository configurations and definitions; tools/triggers retain their loading/ready guards.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: type aliases erase at runtime, account references and fields are preserved, and extracting accountName in descriptor construction does not add serialization or boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository/automation/history sizes and storage/network duration vary. Potentially substantial existing costs are not made more frequent by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression or substantive performance fix; nearby collection-scaled work is pre-existing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sign up for Copilot Free using selected or fallback authentication sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sign-up waits for account initialization, session selection, and a POST response. Session fallback and user-confirmed error retries remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup when the selected account session exists or when no default account exists; two when the selected session lookup falls back.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same provider lookups, filtering, and fallback cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sign-up cannot start its POST until session selection completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST the Copilot Free signup body using available sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one request; up to the fallback session count per attempt if earlier sessions fail, with existing user-confirmed retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same session array reaches the same serial request loop and unchanged small JSON body serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Signup completion awaits response and parsing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normally one selected session; when absent/unavailable, the default provider's session count controls sequential attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The request method tries sessions sequentially and stops at the first successful response; it does not fan out concurrent signup requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getDefaultAccount returns shared initialized state. No new cache is introduced; signup requests retain disableCache:true. Session fallback is unchanged for currently supported accounts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: account ?? undefined preserves the original truthiness branch and all selected session identifiers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fallback session count and request duration are environment-dependent; no new multiplicity or waiting is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; no changed signup fan-out, serialization scale, or retry behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Determine GitHub-backed private extension marketplace eligibility.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Eligibility waits on existing account initialization and then checks the account SKU or enterprise boolean locally.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One account per eligibility check; configured access SKU count for the unchanged includes check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No per-item asynchronous work or new scheduling; the eligibility branch remains constant synchronous work after account availability.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: DefaultAccountService returns stored initialized state. The diff adds no token discovery, metadata cache, invalidation, or external reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: checkAccess receives a non-null account, and the accessor returns that exact object, so the resulting enterprise boolean is identical. Existing telemetry/logging is unchanged and adds no critical-path network request.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Account initialization timing varies; no new expensive operation is present in this eligibility branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; other marketplace authentication providers are not altered by this diff.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 3b381b139291d9bbdd5a5a1ae60d41dad26d137d. Inspected all 11 changed files and every diff page, then traced account initialization, authentication IPC, GitHub transport/queue, affected caches, Agent Host management, filesystem discovery, and collection concurrency as relevant. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions and no concrete performance regression fixes were identified. Static review only; latency and prevalence were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
